sentences.zh: 元康中，京洛童謠曰：「南風起，吹白沙，遙望魯國何嵯峨，千歲髑髏生齒牙。」

translations.literal: In Yuankang the capital children sang: "South wind rises, blows white sand; far off how steep the state of Lu — thousand-year skulls sprout teeth."
translations.idiomatic: In Yuankang the capital children sang: "South wind rises, blows white sand; far off how steep the state of Lu — thousand-year skulls sprout teeth."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「城東馬子莫嚨哅，此至來年纏女閤。」

translations.literal: It also said: "East-city colt, don't whinny — by next year you'll tangle in women's boudoirs."
translations.idiomatic: It also said: "East-city colt, don't whinny — by next year you'll tangle in women's boudoirs."

translations.literal: South wind" is Empress Jia's style name.

translations.idiomatic: White stood for metal — Jin's element.

translations.literal: "Shamen" is the heir apparent's childhood name.

translations.idiomatic: Lu mapped onto Jia Mi's noble seat.

sentences.zh: 言賈后將與謐為亂，以危太子，而趙王因釁咀嚼豪賢，以成篡奪，不得其死之應也。

translations.literal: It means Empress Jia would riot with Mi to endanger the heir, while Prince Zhao would chew up great men and seize the throne — an omen of dying badly.
translations.idiomatic: The gloss tied the verses to Jia's coup plot and Sima Lun's coming slaughter.

sentences.zh: 海西公太和中，百姓歌曰：「青青御路楊，白馬紫遊韁。

translations.literal: Under Duke Haixi's Taihe years the people sang: "Green-green willows on the imperial road — white horse with purple reins.
translations.idiomatic: Under Duke Haixi's Taihe years the people sang: "Green-green willows on the imperial road — white horse with purple reins.

sentences.zh: 汝非皇太子，那得甘露漿？」

translations.literal: You are not crown prince — how get sweet-dew nectar?"
translations.idiomatic: You are not crown prince — how get sweet-dew nectar?"

sentences.zh: 識者曰：「白者，金行，馬者，國族。

translations.literal: Those who understood said: "White is metal phase; horse is the dynastic clan.
translations.idiomatic: Those who understood said: "White is metal phase; horse is the dynastic clan.

sentences.zh: 紫為奪正之色，明以紫間硃也。」

translations.literal: Purple is the hue that usurps orthodoxy — it shows purple wedged between cinnabar."
translations.idiomatic: Purple is the hue that usurps orthodoxy — it shows purple wedged between cinnabar."

sentences.zh: 海西公尋廢，其三子並非海西公之子，縊以馬韁。

translations.literal: Duke Haixi was soon deposed; his three sons were not truly his — they were strangled with horse reins.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi's bastards died by the purple-rein prophecy.

sentences.zh: 死之明日，南方獻甘露馬。

translations.literal: The day after their deaths the south presented a "sweet dew" horse.
translations.idiomatic: A tribute horse arrived ironically named for the nectar line.

finding: s0373 belongs to the complete Haixi Taihe song and its three purported sons, not Minhuai. c0351/c0354/c1360 wrongly attach that reference to the Shamen/Minhuai record. Hold canonical pair pending extraction repair and fresh fingerprinting.
